15 And he said unto them, Take heed, and beware of covetousness: for a man's life consisteth not in the abundance of the things which he possesseth. (Luke 12:15 KJV)

The bible teaches that covetousness is idolatry (Colossians 3:5), and Jesus is teaching that we should be wary of being or acting in idolatry, as it is a sin against God. Our generation should read and believe this principal, as we are in general, an extremely covetousness people, and we tend to idolize our possessions, and lust after the newest inventions. Having many possessions and a lot of money does not mean we are happy, as many rich people are not finding happiness in all their possessions. When we come to the end of our lives, few people will wish they had more possessions or wealth, as they can not take anything with them when they die. It is the spiritual things we will regret, that we did not give more of ourselves, and more of our money, to make a difference in the lives of those we love.

You can not take your money with you when you die, but you can send it on ahead of you while you are on this earth. By investing it into the lives of others, helping the needy, giving to charities, sowing it into the furtherance of the Kingdom of God, and like things. What we do with our time and possessions while in this world, will greatly affect the eternity that we spend with Jesus, so be a good giver while you can, and let it benefit you forever in heaven. As the bible says, be not a hearer of the Word only, but a doer also (James 1:22). Although we, who are born again, are entered into the Lord’s rest, and cease from doing the works of the law, we must do works of faith. As James wrote, faith without works is dead (James 2:20). What good is your faith, if you haven’t any works, or fruit, to show for it? Show you are a Christian by loving one another as Jesus commanded (John 13:35).

Devotional by Pastor Joe W. Green, www.Infinite-Faith.com
